claims.text: The initial material is cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10⁻⁴–10⁻² s⁻¹.
Uncoated, as-cast HfNbTaTiZr has inadequate oxidation resistance for high-temperature use in air.
The proposed intervention is pack aluminizing in an Al-rich pack at 800–900 °C for 2–4 hours under an inert atmosphere.
Pack aluminizing will produce a thin diffusion-barrier coating on cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The aluminized coating will develop a stable Al2O3 surface scale during high-temperature exposure in air.
The resulting Al2O3 scale will be thin and adherent.
The resulting Al2O3 scale will be ductile.
The stable alumina layer will limit oxygen ingress into the underlying alloy.
Limiting oxygen ingress will preserve the alloy's internal microstructure and favorable mechanical properties.
Relative to untreated material, coated samples will exhibit lower oxidation mass gain and a thinner, more adherent oxide scale after exposure at about 1000 °C in air for up to 100 hours.
After oxidation exposure, coated samples will retain room-temperature ductility similar to the untreated as-cast alloy.
After oxidation exposure, coated samples will retain 1000 °C yield strength similar to the untreated as-cast alloy at strain rates of 10⁻⁴–10⁻² s⁻¹.
Maintaining minimal coating–substrate interdiffusion depth is necessary to avoid changing bulk mechanical properties.
The coating is expected to remain effective under both isothermal and cyclic exposure near 1000 °C in air.
The optimal coating thickness and processing window for long-term adherence under cyclic thermal stress are not yet established.
